Implement `check_finding` and `check_routing` in `src/coresight/verify.py`, and add a `trends` parameter to `verify`, so that every test in `tests/test_verify_milestones.py` passes and every test in `tests/test_verify.py` still passes.

Context:
- CoreSight turns photos of drill core trays into a geotechnical log reviewed by a geologist. When the geologist approves a box, agents run. A hole agent (Muse Spark) reads trends that code found between boxes of the drill hole and proposes one action. Then an orchestrator (Muse Wonder) decides which areas of the mine the box concerns (lab, safety, plant, finance). Then each area agent writes a draft, which `verify()` checks.
- Meta's Agents 102 workshop: verify at milestones, not only at the end, with deterministic checks first. These two functions are the milestones before any area agent writes: the hole agent's finding, and the orchestrator's routing. If a check fails, its detail goes back to the model as feedback, so details must be clear sentences without field names.
- Read `tests/test_verify_milestones.py` first: its docstring states every rule, and the tests are the specification. Then read the whole of `src/coresight/verify.py` (you wrote it in earlier sessions: reuse its number extraction and tolerance helpers) and, in `src/coresight/schemas.py`, `HoleTrend`, `RoutingSignals`, `HoleFinding`, `AreaRoute`, `Routing` and `Check`.

- Edit only `src/coresight/verify.py`: the bodies of `check_finding` and `check_routing` (and the last line of their docstrings, "To be built with Muse Code."), plus a new last parameter `trends: list[HoleTrend] = ()` of `verify` whose numbers become candidates of the numbers check. - Do not change the tests, `schemas.py`, other modules or any config.

- Standard library only. Install nothing.
- Do not read or print `.env` or anything under `data/cache` or `data/reviews`. Do not make network calls.
- Match the style of the surrounding code: type hints, small helpers, comments only where the logic is not obvious. Lines up to 100 characters.

When done, run:
- `.venv\Scripts\python -m pytest -q tests/test_verify_milestones.py tests/test_verify.py`

Iterate until both are green, then reply with a short summary of the rules as you implemented them.

Rules as implemented:

- `check_finding` returns `trends`, `action`, `numbers`. Trends: cited kinds must all be in found kinds; unknown use “an RQD drop”, “a weak zone”, “a change of rock”, “sulfides appearing/ending”, no underscores. Action: `none` always passes; with no found trends only `none`; otherwise `oriented_core`/`warn_geotech` need cited `rqd_drop`/`weak_zone`, `sample_contact` needs cited `lithology_change`/`sulfides_appear`/`sulfides_gone`. Numbers: title+body numbers must match runs (current+history), run numbers, box numbers (current+history+trends’ boxes), trends’ `from_m`/`to_m`/RQD fields; a number followed by `%` must match an RQD/TCR candidate, so `12.5 %` fails while `6.0 m` passes. Detail format matches `verify`.
- `check_routing` returns `lab,safety,plant,finance`; missing area fails as “`<Area> has no route`”. Safety must if worst RQD <25 or `rqd_drop`/`weak_zone` present, cannot if RQD≥75 and recovery≥75 with none. Lab must on sulfides, cannot without evidence. Plant must on sulfide appear/gone, cannot with no lithology/sulfide trend and no sulfides. Finance matches lab. Details use the exact “must/cannot apply” sentences from the tests.
